title_options: Model Retirement Errors: Why 'Model Not Found' Is Permanent and Your Retry Loop Cannot Tell
When a Retired Model Returns 404: Classify It Before Your Retry Loop Spends the Budget
Model Gone, 404 Back: Proving Your Retry Policy Stops on a Permanent Model Error
presentation.title_rationale: The selected title frontloads the topic (model retirement errors) and names the reader's problem in the second clause: the retry loop cannot distinguish the permanent condition. It promises one supported benefit - knowing why the loop cannot tell - and does not claim the envelope identifies retirement, which the article explicitly denies.
presentation.long_title_reason: 91 characters. Shortening would drop either the reader problem (the retry loop cannot tell) or the finding (the 404 is permanent); that second clause is what distinguishes this page from the migration guides it links.
presentation.visual_purpose: Two-panel figure drawn only from the measured run: panel 1 shows which envelope fields decide model_unavailable versus rate_limit versus transient and that the same 404 bytes cover a retired ID and a typo; panel 2 shows server-side requests per task per policy from out/retry-policy-compare.csv. It explains the article's central arithmetic (3/3 versus 1/3) and is scoped to the six-row local fixture.
